rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: HSE reports that machinery and plant account for more than 30% of fatal injuries in food and drink manufacturing.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Machinery and plant account for more than 10% of major injuries reported in the food and drink sector.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: HSE's sector page attributes more than 7% of all reportable food-and-drink injuries to machinery and plant.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: The HSE page reports almost 500 machinery-related injuries per year as reportable in the sector data it summarises.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Conveyors were the largest machinery category in the HSE investigation analysis, representing 30% of the cases reviewed.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Fork-lift trucks accounted for 12% and bandsaws for 5% of the machinery incidents in the HSE analysis.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Food machinery safety guidance identifies standards for equipment such as mixers, slicers, packaging machinery and fish-processing machines.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Food machinery should be designed and manufactured so that safety controls also account for hygiene and ease of cleaning.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Food-machinery risk depends on machine type, guarding, access, intervention frequency, cleaning, maintenance, product flow and worker competence.

rows.source: HSE food-processing machinery safety
rows.verified: Food-machinery evidence is machine-, process-, task-, maintenance- and operator-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Hand tools and knives are a major injury source in meat, poultry and fish processing, particularly during boning and cutting tasks.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Heavy or awkward manual handling is identified as a principal cause of injury in the sector.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Wet or greasy floors create a significant slip hazard in meat, poultry and fish processing workplaces.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Conveyors, bandsaws, derinders, skinning and packaging machines are among the machinery hazards listed by HSE.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Fork-lift trucks and loading-bay vehicles create workplace-transport risk in the sector.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Workers may be exposed to cleaning-chemical splashes, vapours and hot objects during production and sanitation.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: HSE identifies Campylobacter exposure in poultry processing as an occupational infection risk.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Aerosolised fish proteins can cause occupational asthma, while smoking processes can create polycyclic-aromatic-hydrocarbon exposure.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Processing risk depends on species, process, knife and machinery use, temperature, hygiene chemicals, biological material and task repetition.

rows.source: HSE meat, poultry and fish processing safety
rows.verified: Meat, poultry and fish evidence is process-, product-, exposure-, equipment- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or illness probability.
